---
title: "cvm_fetch(): the generic API"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment  = "#>"
)
```

`cvm_fetch(dataset, table, ...)` is the single entry point for every
CVM dataset and every table covered by the package.

This article walks through each argument: how issuers are selected
(`cnpj`, `ticker`), how the period is selected (`year` or
`from`/`to`), the `basis` rule for financial statements, the
`validate` and `on_error` modes, and the cache/source plumbing.

`issuer_fetch()`, the entry point of v0.1 and v0.2, is deprecated: it
still works, with a lifecycle warning, and will be removed in a later
release. Its `issuer` argument (CNPJ, CD_CVM, free text or ticker)
and `report_type` map onto the arguments described here.

```{r setup}
library(cvmdata)
```

## Anatomy

```r
cvm_fetch(
  dataset,
  table,
  cnpj     = NULL,
  ticker   = NULL,
  year     = NULL,
  from     = NULL,
  to       = NULL,
  basis    = NULL,
  source   = NULL,
  on_error = "abort",
  validate = "strict",
  ...
)
```

Returns a tibble of subclass `cvm_tbl` carrying seven provenance
attributes (`source`, `fetched_at`, `group`, `dataset`, `table`,
`package_version`, `release`). Column names, table names and categorical values
are preserved in Portuguese as published by CVM; the API surface is
in English.

```{r anatomy}
bb_bpa <- cvm_fetch(
  "dfp", "bpa",
  cnpj = "00.000.000/0001-91",
  year = 2024,
  basis = "ind"
)
bb_bpa

# Provenance:
attr(bb_bpa, "source")
attr(bb_bpa, "dataset")
attr(bb_bpa, "table")
```

## Identifying issuers

`cvm_fetch()` identifies issuers by two keys only, and the two
combine in a single call:

| Argument | Accepts                                              | Match against                                  |
|----------|------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------|
| `cnpj`   | CNPJ, with or without punctuation, vector of any length | `cnpj_cia` / `cnpj_companhia`, punctuation stripped |
| `ticker` | B3 trading code (`PETR4`, `BBAS3`, `BBDC11`)          | `codigo_negociacao` in `fca/valor_mobiliario`, resolved to the issuer's CNPJ |

A CVM code (`"1023"`) or a company name (`"BCO BRASIL"`) passed as
`cnpj` aborts with `cvmdata_error_input`: there is no free-text
search and no CD_CVM lookup in `cvm_fetch()`. To find the CNPJ of a
company you know by name or by CVM code, read the registry, which
carries `cd_cvm`, `denom_social` and `cnpj_cia` side by side:

```{r registry-lookup}
registry <- cvm_fetch("cad", "companhias")
registry[grepl("MAGAZINE LUIZA", registry$denom_social),
         c("cd_cvm", "denom_social", "cnpj_cia")]
```

### CNPJ: punctuated or clean, same rows

```{r identifiers}
# Each call returns identical rows.
a <- cvm_fetch("dfp", "bpa", cnpj = "00.000.000/0001-91",
               year = 2024, basis = "ind")
b <- cvm_fetch("dfp", "bpa", cnpj = "00000000000191",
               year = 2024, basis = "ind")

identical(nrow(a), nrow(b))
```

A CNPJ absent from the table yields zero rows for it, silently — a
miss on a taxpayer id is not a typo the package can second-guess.

### Ticker: resolved through the registration form

A B3 trading code is looked up in `fca/valor_mobiliario` (read from
the same `source` as the data), and the issuer's CNPJ is then
filtered exactly as `cnpj` would be. The lookup reads every yearly
FCA file that carries trading codes (2018 onwards; the column is
empty in earlier files), so the code of a company that has since left
the exchange still resolves, for any `year`: `GOLL4` fetches Gol's
statements of 2019 although the company cancelled its registration in
2026. Tickers cover only exchange-listed securities; a code absent
from every file aborts with `cvmdata_error_input` rather than
returning an empty tibble, and so does a code that maps to more than
one issuer (none does today; pass `cnpj` in that case).

```{r ticker}
petr <- cvm_fetch("dfp", "bpa", ticker = "PETR4",
                  year = 2024, basis = "con")
unique(petr$denom_cia)
```

`cnpj` and `ticker` combine; the result is the union of both sets:

```{r mixed}
two <- cvm_fetch("dfp", "bpa",
                 cnpj = "00.000.000/0001-91",
                 ticker = "MGLU3",
                 year = 2024, basis = "ind")
unique(two$denom_cia)
```

## Selecting the period

Two mutually exclusive forms; passing both aborts.

### Whole years with `year`

`year` is an integer vector of any length (singular naming follows
tidyverse conventions), matching the yearly files the CVM publishes.
`NULL` (default) fetches the **latest available year**, discovered by
HEAD-probing CVM's listing (or from the mirror's inventory). Must be
`NULL` for snapshot tables such as `cad/companhias`.

```{r years-discovery}
# What's published upstream?
cvm_dataset_years("dfp")

# Pass an explicit vector to back-fill history:
history <- cvm_fetch("dfp", "bpa", cnpj = "00.000.000/0001-91",
                     year = 2022:2024, basis = "ind")
sort(unique(format(history$dt_refer, "%Y")))
```

Each CSV publishes `ORDEM_EXERC ∈ {ÚLTIMO, PENÚLTIMO}` — the
declared year and N − 1. The antepenultimate of year N is the last
of year N − 2. `cvm_fetch()` does not synthesize the antepenultimate;
ask for `year = (N - 2):N` if you need it. To read an exercise by its
own year, with the figures originally filed and the comparative of
the following year's file labelled, see [`reading`](#reading) below.

```{r exercise-ordering}
table(history$ordem_exerc)
```

### A date window with `from` and `to`

For slices smaller than a year, pass `from` and `to` together as
complete dates (`"YYYY-MM-DD"` strings or `Date` scalars). Rows are
kept when the document's **reference date** (`dt_refer` in
CAD/ITR/DFP-style tables, `data_referencia` in FRE-style tables)
falls inside the window; the yearly files actually read are the
years the window spans. The reference date is the period the filing
describes, not the day it was delivered.

```{r from-to}
# ITR balance sheets referenced in the first half of 2024
h1 <- cvm_fetch("itr", "bpa", cnpj = "00.000.000/0001-91",
                from = "2024-01-01", to = "2024-06-30",
                basis = "con")
unique(h1$dt_refer)
```

Incomplete dates (`"2024"`, `"2024-06"`) are rejected, as is a
window on a snapshot table. One bound without the other aborts; for
whole years use `year`.

### Partial failure with `on_error`

When several yearly files are read (more than one element in `year`,
or a window spanning several years), `on_error = "warn"` keeps
surviving years and emits `cvmdata_warn_partial_failure` listing
failures. `on_error = "silent"` does the same without the warning.
`on_error = "abort"` (default) aborts at the first HTTP failure.
Total failure (every year fails) always aborts regardless.
Single-year calls, non-yearly tables (CAD) and the implicit
`year = NULL` fallback always abort on HTTP failure.

Parse and schema-validation failures are governed by `validate`, not
by `on_error` — schema drift is treated as a separate signal.

## `basis`

Eight tables in ITR/DFP publish both **individual** and **consolidated**
variants of the same concept (`bpa`, `bpp`, `dre`, `dra`, `dfc_md`,
`dfc_mi`, `dmpl`, `dva`). `basis` is **required** for those, with no
default: many issuers file only individual statements, so defaulting
to `"con"` would silently drop them.

```{r basis-required, error = TRUE}
cvm_fetch("dfp", "bpa", cnpj = "00.000.000/0001-91", year = 2024)
```

`basis` takes `"ind"`, `"con"` or `c("ind", "con")`. With both, the
two variants are read and stacked. Whatever you ask for, those eight
tables **always carry a `basis` column** in the result, so a single
value and a stacked pair have the same shape:

```{r basis-both}
both <- cvm_fetch("dfp", "bpa", cnpj = "00.000.000/0001-91",
                  year = 2024, basis = c("ind", "con"))
table(both$basis)
"basis" %in% names(bb_bpa)
```

On every other table (`companhias`, `submissao`, `parecer`,
`composicao_capital`, every FRE/FCA detail table) `basis` must be
left unset; passing it aborts rather than being ignored:

```{r basis-forbidden, error = TRUE}
cvm_fetch("dfp", "composicao_capital",
          cnpj = "00.000.000/0001-91", year = 2024,
          basis = "ind")
```

## `reading`

The same eight tables carry two columns of figures per account in
every yearly file: `ordem_exerc = "ÚLTIMO"`, the exercise the file is
about, and `ordem_exerc = "PENÚLTIMO"`, the comparative the issuer
presented for the previous exercise. That comparative is often
**restated** — after a change of accounting policy, an error, a
reorganisation — and it is the figure later statements build on.
Measured on the DFP, about a third of the issuers restate: Porto
Seguro's consolidated total assets of 2022 are R$ 50.5 bn in the 2022
file and R$ 39.9 bn in the 2023 one.

`reading` reads an exercise by its own year and labels the two
readings. `"original"` is the `ÚLTIMO` rows of the file of `year`;
`"restated"` is the `PENÚLTIMO` rows of the file of `year + 1`, which
the call reads on its own; `c("original", "restated")` stacks both.
Rows come as published, with a `reading` column appended:

```{r reading-both}
pssa <- cvm_fetch("dfp", "bpa", ticker = "PSSA3",
                  year = 2022, basis = "con",
                  reading = c("original", "restated"))
pssa[pssa$cd_conta == "1",
     c("dt_refer", "ordem_exerc", "dt_fim_exerc", "vl_conta", "reading")]
```

`dt_refer` and `versao` are those of the document each row came from
(the restated row is dated 2023); `dt_fim_exerc` — and `dt_ini_exerc`
in the flow statements — identify the exercise, so the two readings
pair on the issuer, the exercise dates, `cd_conta` and, in `dmpl`,
`coluna_df`. Either reading can be missing for an issuer that stopped
or started filing between the two years, and the restated figure is
whatever the issuer presented: the banks that adopted CMN Resolution
4,966 in 2025 presented no comparative for 2024 on the individual
basis, and their restated reading of 2024 is a column of zeros, as in
the CVM file.

An exercise whose following year's file is not published yet has no
restated reading; the call says so and returns what exists. When the
file exists but the issuer has not filed in it yet (the current year's
file opens with the first non-December fiscal years), the restated
rows are simply absent:

```{r reading-latest}
latest <- cvm_fetch("dfp", "bpa", ticker = "PSSA3", year = 2025,
                    basis = "con", reading = c("original", "restated"))
table(latest$reading)
```

With `from`/`to`, the window applies to the exercise end
(`dt_fim_exerc`) rather than to the document date, so an exercise's
two readings stay together. Without `reading` (the default) each file
comes as the CVM publishes it, `ÚLTIMO` and `PENÚLTIMO` rows together,
and there is no `reading` column. In the ITR, the comparative of the
balance sheet (`bpa`, `bpp`) is the previous year end, not the previous
year's quarter, so the restated reading of an ITR balance sheet is the
year-end balance as the following year's quarterly filings present it;
the flow statements (`dre`, `dfc_*`, `dva`, `dmpl`) compare like with
like.

## `validate`

Controls the strictness of schema validation at parse time. Three
modes:

| Mode       | Table with META published         | Table with `meta_status: missing`                  |
|------------|------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------|
| `"strict"` | Validates; mismatch aborts.        | Aborts with `cvmdata_error_meta_unavailable`.      |
| `"warn"`   | Validates; mismatch warns.         | Warns with `cvmdata_warn_meta_unavailable`; data returned. |
| `"skip"`   | Skips validation silently.         | Skips silently.                                    |

The eight FRE tables without published META (`empregado_PCD`,
`empregado_local_declaracao_genero`, etc.) need `validate = "warn"`
or `"skip"` to be readable. See the **fre** article for a worked
example.

## Cache, TTL and source backend

Downloaded artefacts are cached under
`tools::R_user_dir("cvmdata", "cache")`. Each ZIP / CSV stores an
ETag/Last-Modified sidecar; HTTP revalidation is throttled by a
30-day TTL (configurable via `options(cvmdata.cache_ttl_seconds)`).
Cached units are LRU-evicted once total size exceeds the limit set
by `options(cvmdata.cache_max_size_mb)` (default 100 MiB).

```{r cache-info}
info <- cvm_cache_info()
info
attr(info, "total_size_bytes")
```

`source` selects the backend: from v0.1.0 the default is `"mirror"`,
which reads parquet snapshots from GitHub Releases via DuckDB with
year-partition filter pushdown; `"cvm"` reads the open-data portal
over HTTP and remains fully supported. The current backend is read by
`cvm_source_get()` and changed at session scope by `cvm_source_set()`:

```{r source}
cvm_source_get()
```
